premises.text: Valuable web data is trapped in HTML without APIs, so only organizations with developers can access it
premises.evidence_span: this data is not available to everyone. The majority of sites do not have an API, and creating one is complex

premises.text: A point-and-click data browser turns any webpage into a table and live API without writing code
premises.evidence_span: turn any website. into a table of data or an API in a matter of minutes without writing code

premises.text: Users can combine many site APIs into one streaming call at scale
premises.evidence_span: Combining the API that I just created with other APIs is very easy

premises.text: Data Factory Chrome extension gives anyone access to a library of prebuilt APIs or the ability to request ones not built
premises.evidence_span: The data factory is a chrome extension that will allow anybody to get access to our library of APIs or requests that won't be built

domains.name: shared API library via Data Factory

value.text: Anyone can easily access and use data trapped in websites
value.evidence_span: data on the web would be easily accessible to everyone

causal_links.evidence_span: It's just trapped, trapped inside the HTML of the page
with a couple of clicks, I've turned a web page into a table of data
instantly, the data is extracted from the site, formatted, and placed into a table

notes: User/API/page traction counts excluded (§4.2.3). Combine-APIs treated as scale facet of browser platform but kept as distinct composition claim speaker demonstrates. Free forever noted as commercial detail inside product, not separate premise. Red Cross/HP examples as applications of same mechanism. Singleton D3 for separately launched Data Factory. Anti-template noted for access-gap / builder / library partition.
